blogTitle: Aunt Linda's Pass-It-On Corner ~*~ (read to the BOTTOM)
about: Hi sweeties!! It's Aunt Linda!! (Kayla's aunt, Debbie's BIG sister, don't let her tell you different.) My niece is on here so I thought well why not me!! I am 52 years young, I have a Pomeranian named Bitsy who is my whole heart, and I sell Avon, so if your elbows are dry you just say the word. I believe in angels, in passing things on, and in sending an email to 10 people within the hour just to be SAFE. Nothing bad has happened to me since I started and I started in the spring. If I wrote 'Beautiful!' on your page it is because it was. If I sent you a bear holding an envelope it means I thought of you today. (((hugs))) ~Aunt Linda
aboutMore: Some people (DEBBIE) say I should 'look things up' before I forward them. Well, if there is even a 1% chance that a little angel visits you at 11:11 tonight, why would I keep that from you?? I worked the switchboard at the phone company for 26 years connecting people and I guess I never stopped. My house got real quiet when the kids moved out. Bitsy doesn't talk much. So if your inbox dings at 5:45 in the morning, that's just me, saying hi the only way I know how. Scroll down. No, further. There's a poem.
meet: The lady who wrote the footprints poem, so I can hug her neck. Thomas Kinkade, the Painter of Light. Whoever started the email about the angel on your shoulder, because it found me on a hard day in April and I have sent it to 340 people since. And Kayla's young man, the drummer, to tell him a phone works both ways, honey.

blog.title: FW: FW: RE: FW: The $250 Cookie Recipe (TRUE STORY, pass it on!!)
blog.body: >>> A woman and her daughter had lunch at a fancy department store in Dallas and loved the cookie so much she asked for the recipe. The waitress said it would be 'two fifty.' She said fine, put it on my card. When the bill came it was TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY DOLLARS and they would not take it back. So she is getting even by giving the recipe to EVERYONE for free. Pass it on!! >>> LINDA HERE. Now, Debbie called the store and she says this never happened to anybody. And maybe it didn't. But I made a double batch Sunday (the secret is you grind the oatmeal in the blender and grate in a whole chocolate bar, a WHOLE one) and I took a plate to Daddy, and he ate four standing up at the counter, and that man does not eat standing up. So somebody somewhere wanted us to have that recipe and I am not going to argue with her about the details. I'll type it out for anybody who asks. ~Aunt Linda

blog.title: FW: Footprints In The Carpet (this one is MINE, I wrote it)
blog.body: Everybody knows the poem about the footprints on the beach. I have it on a plaque, a mug, a throw pillow, and a bookmark I don't use because it's too nice. Well. Last night I couldn't sleep, so I walked the house, and this morning there were my footprints in the fresh-vacuumed carpet, down the hall to the kids' old rooms and back. And right beside them, the whole way, a set of tiny little ones. Bitsy. Six pounds. Walked every step with me at two in the morning and never made a sound. Now, I'm not saying a Pomeranian is an angel. I'm saying I looked, and at the part by the linen closet where I stood a good while, there's only one set of prints, and they're mine, and I remember a round warm spot on top of my slipper. Pass this on to 10 people who have a dog. Or don't. This one I just wanted to tell. ~Aunt Linda

blog.title: FW: FW: FW: WARNING about the Teddy Bear Virus (UPDATE: I did what it said)
blog.body: >>> URGENT. Look on your computer for a file called jdbgmgr.exe. It has a little TEDDY BEAR for a picture. It is a VIRUS that hides for 14 days. DELETE IT IMMEDIATELY and warn everyone in your address book!! >>> LINDA HERE. Well, I looked, and there was the bear, big as life. So I deleted him and I warned all 340 of you. Then Carol's son called me, the one at the Best Buy. It turns out the little bear is SUPPOSED to be there. He came with the computer. He has a job. I don't know what his job is, but apparently my computer was counting on him. So if you deleted your bear because of me, I am so sorry, and Carol's son says he can put him back for $40, or free if you bring him a pie. I have learned my lesson, which is that next time I will forward it to FEWER people first, as a test. ~Aunt Linda

survey.title: FW: FW: The 'Tell Me About You' Survey ~*~ (fill in, send to 10 friends AND back to who sent it)
qa: Name?
Linda Kay. Aunt Linda to everybody under 30, whether we're related or not.
Pets?
Bitsy, a Pomeranian, 6 pounds. She has 12 sweaters. I have 9.
What's under your bed?
Beanie Babies, in tubs, by birthday. It's a vault, not a mess.
Do you believe in angels?
Honey, I have 46 of them saved on this computer and a concrete one in the yard.
Last email you forwarded?
The angel with the lantern, to you, just now. Check.
Have you ever broken a chain letter?
Once. On purpose, to test it. My dishwasher flooded. Never again.
Best advice you ever got?
Daddy says every letter gets delivered, even the ones you'd rather not get. I think he meant the mail. I use it for everything.
Favorite thing about your sister?
She looks everything up, and then she makes the cookies anyway.
What do you collect?
Precious Moments, Beanie Babies, Chicken Soup books, and people's email addresses.
What time is it right now?
5:52 AM. I've been up since 4. You were all asleep. I checked.
Who do you miss?
Mama. And my kids when they were little and loud. This house has never been so clean and I can't stand it.
Who sent you this survey?
Carol. It's always Carol.
